newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro bourses climb after US rates move.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro bourses climb after US rates move.

text.p: European bourses climbed sharply on Wednesday, with Frankfurt hitting a record high as a suprise U.S. decision to leave interest rates unchanged removed market uncertainty.

The dollar slowly clawed back some of its losses suffered when currency markets, which had priced in a 0.25 percent percentage point rise in U.S. rates, were caught out by the U.S. central bank's decision to leave rates alone on Tuesday.

Analysts said the U.S. move was a calculated gamble that the American economy will slow before inflation starts to rise. But it disappointed foreign exchanges where higher rates would have made dollar-based assets more attractive to investors.
Stocks in London and Paris put on a healthy performance, encouraged by a positive opening on Wall Street, but the star was Frankfurt which continued a bull-run to finish floor trade at a new peak.
A wave of buying of German stocks pushed up the DAX index to end at 2,658.97, eclipsing the previous best close of 2,646.10 set on September 20.
Traders who had sold off shares in anticipation of an increase in U.S. interest rates went back into the market to buy at the decision to leave the rates unchanged.
In London, Europe's biggest bourse, stocks climbed 0.6 percent, recovering from three day's of losses and taking heart from gains in U.S. Treasury bonds after the rate decision.
"There has been obvious relief that the Fed did nothing and we have seen a few buyers again this morning," said one trader.
In the previous three sessions the FTSE 100 index dropped some 64 points from its near-record high of 3,974.3 on September 19.
Some traders saw the market's strength continuing.
Said Robin Griffiths, chart specialist at HSBC James Capel: "The UK is...close to a golden scenario, being good value and backed by the strongest economic growth in Europe."
But the U.S. decision to leave interest rates unchanged disappointed some investors, who feared U.S. rates will have to be raised even more later, traders said.
Paris shares also did well, climbing 1.21 percent, helped by the American decision to hold interest rates.
"It looks like the Fed's move gives the bourse a month and a half of breathing space," until after the U.S. presidential election, a trader said.

Traders said the market was holding up well, with demand emerging at every dip, but they said investors were carefully watching Wall Street's reactions, the dollar's level and news about the health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin.
The dollar staged something of a recovery after falling by a pfennig against the mark as the failure to raise rates disappointed forex markets.
By early afternoon, the dollar had regained its composure and was trading at 1.5103 marks, compared with Tuesday's figure of 1.5131 in late Europe. It also strengthened about a yen.

"We had the big sell-off overnight and there's some good support coming in around the 1.5020/30 area -- we're really waiting to see what New York does," said a proprietary trader at a merchant bank in London.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5103 marks and 110.32 yen compared with 1.5131 marks and 109.79 yen in Europe late on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 22.3 points up at 3,932.8.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was 24.74 points up at 2,106.24.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt ended up 20.52 at 2,658.97. PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $382.40 an ounce compared to the London closing of $382.05 on Tuesday. Silver was at $4.92, up three cents.
